portuguese-ceylon.t: The Portuguese colony on the coasts of Sri Lanka, created by the bequest of the last Kotte king and lost to the Dutch.
portuguese-ceylon.o: The Portuguese had held a fort at Colombo since the early 16th century and dominated the [[s:kingdom-of-kotte|Kingdom of Kotte]]. When its Christian king Dharmapala died in 1597, the Portuguese Crown claimed his realm under his will, making the Sinhalese lowlands a colony; Jaffna was added in 1619.
portuguese-ceylon.r: The colony was administered by a captain-general at Colombo under the [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] of [[s:portuguese-india|Portuguese India]]. The Portuguese drew revenue from [[e:cinnamon|cinnamon]], collected by Salagama peelers as a service obligation, and from areca and elephants. Catholic missions converted many coastal people, especially fishing communities, and Portuguese words entered Sinhala and Tamil. Repeated campaigns against the [[s:kingdom-of-kandy|Kingdom of Kandy]] failed.
portuguese-ceylon.e: The [[s:dutch-east-india-company-territories|Dutch East India Company]], allied with Rajasinha II of Kandy, captured Galle in 1640, Colombo in 1656 and Jaffna in 1658, ending Portuguese rule. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] kept the coast, creating [[s:dutch-ceylon|Dutch Ceylon]].

cr.a: myself, based on ancient national symbol.

prince-bishopric-of-constance.t: The temporal lordship of the bishops of Germany's largest medieval diocese, ruled from Meersburg after the Reformation drove them from Constance.
prince-bishopric-of-constance.o: Constance became a bishopric around 600, serving the [[s:alemanni|Alemanni]], and grew into the largest diocese of the German lands, stretching from the [[e:alps|Alps]] to the Neckar. In 1155 [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] confirmed the [[e:bishop|bishop]]'s possessions and rights, the basis of a small secular territory around Lake Constance.
prince-bishopric-of-constance.r: The city of Constance became an imperial city independent of its [[e:bishop|bishop]] and hosted the Council of Constance from 1414 to 1418, which ended the Western Schism and burned Jan Hus. The bishops acquired the Reichenau abbey in 1540. After Constance became Protestant in 1527, they moved to Meersburg, where they built a baroque New Palace.
prince-bishopric-of-constance.e: In 1803 the prince-bishopric was secularised and its lands went to Baden. The diocese itself was dissolved in 1821, its parts divided between the new Archdiocese of Freiburg and Swiss dioceses.

portuguese-syriam.t: A Portuguese adventurer's private fief at the port of Syriam in Lower Burma, which lasted fourteen years before the Burmese retook it.
portuguese-syriam.o: Filipe de Brito e Nicote, a Portuguese [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] in the service of the king of the [[s:mrauk-u-kingdom|Mrauk U Kingdom]], was placed in charge of the port of Syriam, near present-day Yangon, after the fall of Pegu in 1599. He soon turned it into his own base, obtained backing from the Portuguese [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]] in [[e:goa|Goa]] and was recognised as its governor.
portuguese-syriam.r: De Brito ruled with a small Portuguese garrison and local allies, collecting customs on the [[e:rice|rice]] and [[e:timber|timber]] trade and controlling access to the Irrawaddy. He built a fort and church, encouraged Catholic conversions and allied with local Mon leaders. He was notorious among Burmese for looting pagodas to melt down their bells for [[e:field-artillery|cannon]].
portuguese-syriam.e: Anaukpetlun of the [[s:restored-toungoo-kingdom|Restored Toungoo Kingdom]] besieged Syriam in 1613 and took it after a few months. De Brito was executed by impalement, and the Portuguese captives were resettled in Upper [[s:myanmar|Burma]] as royal gunners, where their descendants, the Bayingyi, still live.

principality-of-albania.t: Albania's first internationally recognised state, a principality that survived foreign occupation in the First World War and was rebuilt as a nation in 1920.
principality-of-albania.o: The Conference of Ambassadors in [[e:london|London]] made [[s:albania|Albania]] an independent principality under the Great Powers' guarantee and chose the German Prince Wilhelm of Wied as ruler. He arrived in Durrës on 7 March 1914, replacing the [[s:provisional-government-of-albania|Provisional Government of Albania]] and Essad Pasha's [[s:republic-of-central-albania|Republic of Central Albania]].
principality-of-albania.r: Wied's rule collapsed within months amid Essad's intrigues, a Muslim peasant revolt in central [[s:albania|Albania]] and Greek-backed autonomy in the south; he left in September 1914. During the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] Italian, Austrian, Serbian, Greek and French troops occupied the country. The Congress of Lushnjë in 1920 created a regency council, moved the capital to Tirana and secured [[e:league-of-nations|League of Nations]] membership.
principality-of-albania.e: The 1920s saw instability, with Fan Noli's June Revolution of 1924 overthrown by Ahmet Zogu in December. In January 1925 a constituent assembly abolished the principality and created the [[s:albanian-republic|Albanian Republic]], with Zogu as president.
principality-of-albania.re: Sunni Islam, Orthodox and Catholic Christianity

principality-of-schwarzenberg.t: Franconian territory of the Schwarzenberg family, whose princes became some of the greatest landowners and statesmen of the Habsburg monarchy.
principality-of-schwarzenberg.o: The lords of Seinsheim took the name Schwarzenberg from a castle near Scheinfeld in Franconia in the 15th century. In 1599 the family was raised to the rank of imperial counts, and in 1670 Johann Adolf von Schwarzenberg, a senior adviser of Emperor Leopold I, was made a prince of the Empire, with the lands around Scheinfeld forming the core of the family's immediate territory.
principality-of-schwarzenberg.r: The Franconian lands were small, but the family's real weight lay in service to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and in vast estates acquired in [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]], including Frauenberg (Hluboká), bought in 1661, and Krumau (Český Krumlov), inherited from the Eggenberg family in 1719. The territory was Catholic and administered by officials while the princes lived at court in [[e:vienna|Vienna]] or on their Bohemian estates.
principality-of-schwarzenberg.e: In 1806 the Franconian lands were mediatised and placed under the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]]. The family remained prominent: Karl Philipp zu Schwarzenberg commanded the allied armies at Leipzig in 1813, and Felix zu Schwarzenberg led the [[e:austrian-empire|Austrian Empire's]] government after the 1848 revolution.

plymouth-colony.t: The settlement founded by the Mayflower Pilgrims in 1620, remembered for the Mayflower Compact and the 1621 harvest feast with the Wampanoag.
plymouth-colony.o: English Separatists who had left the Church of [[e:england|England]], many of them after years of exile in Leiden, sailed on the Mayflower in 1620 and landed at Plymouth on Cape Cod Bay. Before landing, 41 men signed the Mayflower Compact, agreeing to form a civil body politic. Half the settlers died in the first winter.
plymouth-colony.r: The Pilgrims survived with help from the [[s:wampanoag-confederacy|Wampanoag Confederacy]], whose sachem Massasoit made an alliance with them in 1621. William Bradford, governor for most years until 1657, wrote the history Of Plymouth Plantation. The colony had no royal charter, governing itself through an annual General Court of freemen, and lived by farming, fishing and the [[e:fur-trade|fur trade]]. It remained small, with perhaps 7,000 people by 1690.
plymouth-colony.e: King Philip's War in 1675 to 1676 devastated the colony. It was absorbed into the [[s:dominion-of-new-england|Dominion of New England]] in 1686, and after that collapsed, the charter of 1691 merged Plymouth into the [[s:province-of-massachusetts-bay|Province of Massachusetts Bay]].

political-committee-of-national-liberati.t: The 'Mountain Government' created by the Greek resistance in 1944, which held the first Greek elections in which women voted.
political-committee-of-national-liberati.o: By 1944 the left-wing resistance movement EAM and its army ELAS controlled much of mountainous [[e:greece|Greece]]. On 10 March 1944 EAM created the Political Committee of National Liberation (PEEA) at Viniani in Evrytania, as a rival to both the collaborationist [[s:hellenic-state-1941-1944|Hellenic State]] and the government-in-exile in [[e:cairo|Cairo]].
political-committee-of-national-liberati.r: PEEA was led first by Colonel Evripidis Bakirtzis and then by the law professor Alexandros Svolos. It organised local self-government, people's courts and schools in liberated areas, and in April 1944 held elections for a National Council, which met at Koryschades; women voted for the first time in [[e:greece|Greece]]. The Greek forces in [[e:egypt|Egypt]] mutinied in its support.
political-committee-of-national-liberati.e: At the [[s:lebanese-republic|Lebanon]] Conference in May 1944, PEEA agreed to join a government of national unity under Georgios Papandreou, and its ministers entered that government in September. It dissolved after liberation in November 1944, shortly before fighting in [[s:athens|Athens]] began.

principality-of-chach.t: The early medieval principality of the Tashkent oasis, a Sogdian-Turkic borderland whose ruler's execution helped bring about the Battle of Talas.
principality-of-chach.o: Chach, or Shash, was the oasis on the Chirchiq River where Tashkent now stands. It emerged as a principality in the 6th century, closely tied to the [[s:western-turkic-khaganate|Western Turkic Khaganate]], whose rulers often installed Turkic tuduns or relatives as local lords alongside a Sogdian-speaking population.
principality-of-chach.r: Chach controlled a fertile irrigated plain at the meeting point of farmland and steppe, trading with Turkic nomads and producing [[e:silver|silver]] and weapons. Its coins blended Sogdian and Turkic features, and the ruling house bore Turkic titles. Chinese sources call it Shi, the 'stone' country.
principality-of-chach.e: In 750 the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] general [[e:gao|Gao]] Xianzhi executed the ruler of Chach, whose son sought help from the [[e:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasids]]; the resulting [[e:battle-of-talas|Battle of Talas]] in 751 ended Chinese influence west of the Tian Shan. Chach then came under Muslim rule, later as part of the [[s:samanid-empire|Samanid Empire]].

peoples-state-of-reuss.t: Brief Thuringian republic uniting the two old Reuss principalities before they merged into Thuringia.
peoples-state-of-reuss.o: The Principality of [[s:principality-of-reuss-greiz|Reuss Elder Line]] at Greiz and the Principality of [[s:principality-of-reuss-gera|Reuss Younger Line]] at Gera both became free states in November 1918 after their princes abdicated. In April 1919 the two united as the People's State of Reuss, with Gera as capital.
peoples-state-of-reuss.r: The state was industrial, with textile and machine-building works around Gera and Greiz, and its politics were dominated by the Social Democrats and Independent Socialists. It existed mainly to manage the transition from monarchy and to negotiate the union of the small Thuringian states.
peoples-state-of-reuss.e: On 1 May 1920 the People's State of Reuss merged with six other states to form the [[s:free-state-of-thuringia|Free State of Thuringia]]. Gera, its capital, became one of Thuringia's main industrial cities and later a district capital in East [[e:germany|Germany]].

prince-bishopric-of-verden.t: Small church principality between the Weser and Elbe, rooted in Charlemagne's conquest of the Saxons and handed to Sweden in 1648.
prince-bishopric-of-verden.o: The diocese of [[e:verden|Verden]] was founded around 800 in the wake of [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne's]] wars against the [[s:saxons|Saxons]]. Its [[e:bishop|bishops]] acquired estates on the Aller and the lower Weser. After the fall of Henry the Lion in 1180 they ruled a secular territory as imperial princes, though their cathedral city of Verden was largely self-governing and they resided at Rotenburg.
prince-bishopric-of-verden.r: The territory was a thinly settled land of heath and moor. Its [[e:bishop|bishops]] were usually drawn from the princely houses of northern [[e:germany|Germany]], especially Brunswick-Lüneburg. The [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] spread in the 16th century, and Lutheran administrators such as Philip Sigismund of [[s:principality-of-wolfenbuttel|Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel]] replaced Catholic bishops. In the [[e:thirty-years-war|Thirty Years War]] the see was held by the Danish prince Frederick, later Frederick III of [[e:denmark|Denmark]].
prince-bishopric-of-verden.e: The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 secularised the see as the Duchy of [[e:verden|Verden]] and gave it to [[e:sweden|Sweden]], which ruled it with [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]]. [[e:denmark|Denmark]] seized it in 1712 and sold it to the [[s:electorate-of-hanover|Electorate of Hanover]] in 1715. It is now in Lower Saxony.

proto-kingdom-of-nekhen.t: The predynastic chiefdom of Hierakonpolis, home of the falcon god Horus and one of the cradles of Egyptian kingship.
proto-kingdom-of-nekhen.o: Nekhen, the Greek Hierakonpolis, lay on the west bank of the [[e:nile|Nile]] in southern [[e:upper-egypt|Upper Egypt]] and was among the largest settlements of the Naqada period. By c. 3500 BCE it had a ceremonial precinct, breweries, pottery kilns and an elite cemetery, and its chiefs controlled trade with [[e:nubia|Nubia]] and along desert routes to the south.
proto-kingdom-of-nekhen.r: Nekhen was the cult centre of Horus, the falcon god later embodied by every Egyptian king. Its Tomb 100, the 'Painted Tomb', bears the earliest known Egyptian wall painting, with boats, hunting scenes and a figure smiting captives. Excavations have revealed an oval ceremonial court and an elite cemetery with buried animals, including elephants, hippopotami and baboons, signs of an ambitious ruling ideology.
proto-kingdom-of-nekhen.e: Around 3150 BCE its rulers seem to have merged with, or been overtaken by, the kings of the [[s:proto-kingdom-of-thinis|Proto-kingdom of Thinis]]. The town remained a royal religious centre: the Narmer Palette and the Scorpion Macehead were found in its temple's Main Deposit, and Nekhen stayed the symbolic capital of [[e:upper-egypt|Upper Egypt]].
